lane: sponsor-i18n (item 5, R7 backlog) — retitled post-panel to delegate-mode i18n (R9)

panel.description: Joint round-grade adversarial panel over items 4 (delegate-flow) + 5 (sponsor-i18n) dossiers, run 2026-08-28. 4 cross-family seats filesystem/inline-armed + 1 independent verification pass. This is a JOINT panel — the same register applies to both lanes; each lane applies only the rows tagged for it (or [J]).

verification_note: Conductor re-verified every contested claim against the live tree before disposition. The agy-vs-qwen conflict over the Indonesian phrase "atas nama" (agy: implies formal legal proxy/kuasa, should be banned; qwen: reused it in its own counter-proposed copy) was resolved least-claim-wins in favor of agy — banning the phrase is the narrower, more conservative change, and Indonesian legal/immigration register treats "atas nama" as carrying power-of-attorney connotations this flow does not have. R21 point (v) — kimi's claim that research/design/mockups/sponsor-i18n/delegate-i18n.html does not exist — is REJECTED as a panel-setup artifact, not a real defect: the file exists on this lane's branch (commit d0974126a shipped both delegate-i18n.html and delegate-i18n.body.html); kimi's filesystem-armed seat was only handed the .body.html copy in its review packet, so it never saw the wrapped file.
note_on_rows: The 27 rows below are the JOINT disposition register, copied faithfully from the panel's shared register file — identical to the rows recorded in the sibling delegate-flow lane's own adversarial.json. Each row's tag ([D]=delegate-flow lane only, [I]=sponsor-i18n lane only, [J]=both) shows which lane(s) it targets. This lane (I) applied every [I] and [J] row assigned to it by the conductor; rows tagged [D]-only (e.g. R3, R4, R5, R7, R8, R10, R11, R15, R20, R24, R25, R27) were left unapplied here by design — they belong to the sibling lane's own dossier, not this one.

rows.text: I's mockup Screen 4 says "the traveller can delete this check at any time" / "wisatawan dapat menghapus…kapan saja" — false twice: the right is bound to the session cookie (286:99; garuda_voa_public.py:578,590-595 — normally the DELEGATE's browser) and no deletion UI exists. Rewrite: actor = the session-holder ("whoever ran this check can delete it from this browser and session"); add §4 acceptance: deletion copy never names an actor the session model cannot reach.

The 3rd gate option ("arranging for someone else, or for more than one person") is NOT equivalent to NOT_SELF_PAY ∪ GROUP_CASE — a supported delegate IS literally "arranging for someone else", and no travellers/self_pay fact is collected at that point. Rewrite §3.1: the gate asks EXPLICIT facts (option copy anchored to payment and traveller count, per agy F8's three-option phrasing), routes only on the owner-defined exclusions, never on a vague label.

Early-exit screen must NOT reuse the literal decline copy: "You told us someone else is paying" / "travelling with {N} people" would be false (facts never declared, {N} unknown). Author a generic early-exit mirror; specific copy only after the underlying facts are explicitly declared. §3.7 amended.

Mode ambiguity: middle option says the traveller "will answer for themselves" but downstream copy renders third-person with the delegate as declarant. Split cleanly in §3.1/§3.2: helper-operates mode keeps the traveller as addressed declarant where feasible; delegate-answers mode uses delegate attestation + third person. State which one the middle option IS (delegate-answers, per R5b's own confirm copy) and fix the option wording accordingly.
